title: Al-Khaliq, the Creator
hookLine: the Creator, who plans and brings into being
tomorrow: three making names in one verse. why not just one?

lines: A PLAN, BEFORE ANYTHING IS MADE.
cards: Before any group trip, the chat fills up with a plan: who drives, who brings what, a shared doc nobody opens. And somebody always types: wait, are we sure about this?
The Qur'an has a moment like that at the start of the human story. Before anything is made, Allah tells the angels the plan. In Pickthall's words: "Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth."
And the angels push back: "Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood?" A fair question. What comes back?

teach.h: I KNOW THAT WHICH YE KNOW NOT.
teach.b: The answer is one line: "Surely I know that which ye know not." No speech, no list of reasons. The plan stands.
That's where today's name begins. Al-Khaliq, the Creator.
Al-Ghazali, in his book on the names, says creating starts with planning and measuring, before anything exists, the way a builder settles the design before the first brick.
Then comes the bringing into being, and the Qur'an says how short that step is for Him: "His command, when He intendeth a thing, is only that He saith unto it: Be! and it is."

teach.h: FIRST THE PLAN, THEN BE! AND IT IS.
teach.b: Plan, then be. Now look at who the plan was for. The viceroy in the story is Adam, and through him, everyone.

teach.h: ONE SOUL, THEN ALL OF US.
teach.b: Surah four opens: "O mankind! Be careful of your duty to your Lord Who created you from a single soul." One soul, and from it a multitude of men and women.
In the Qur'an's telling, every family tree on your street starts on the same first page.
So here's the detail to tell a friend tonight: before the first human was made, the angels asked whether people were a good idea, and the answer was a plan, and trust in the Planner.
People plan things too, and make things. The Qur'an keeps the name al-Khaliq for the One who made all of it, and the planning came first.

how: Muslims call on God by His names in du'a and remembrance; al-Khaliq, the Creator, is named in the Qur'an, and the story of the angels and the viceroy is recited in surah al-Baqarah.

o: the One who keeps the world running each day
the One who judges people at the end of time
the One who plans and brings things into being

games.q: the first plan — tap the pairs.
p: the Creator, who plans and makes
how short the making is for Him

s: in the story, the angels were rebelling against God
they asked a question, saying they hymn His praise. the answer: I know that which ye know not.
al-Ghazali says creating begins with planning, before anything exists
first the measuring and the design, then the bringing into being.
the Qur'an traces all people back to a single soul
surah four: created you from a single soul, and from it a multitude of men and women.

games.q: you're one of the angels. you've just heard the plan: a viceroy on the earth, one who might do harm. what does the text have the angels do?
o: ask their question out loud, then hear: I know what you know not.
stay silent, since angels never ask God anything at all.
refuse to go along until they're given every reason.
games.why: they ask, honestly. and the answer isn't an argument; it's a plan, and the knowledge of the One who made it.

practice: Choose one good thing you could bring about this week, something small: a meal for someone, a call you keep putting off. Name the wish in one line, then the one thing most likely to get in the way, then your plan for when it does.
Hold that plan quietly through the sit, the way a builder holds the drawing before the first brick.

wordCard.voice: Al-Khaliq: the Creator, the One who plans and brings into being. In the story, the plan came first, and it was for every one of us.

orig.note: Arabic: the Creator. named in surah 59 beside al-Bari' and al-Musawwir.

carryVoice: Keep this close: he creates, and the plan came before the clay. See you tomorrow.
